rationale: M14 IMPORTS_ENUM gap 2. A re-export is a MODULE DEPENDENCY as well as an export: `export { a } from "./m"` cannot be evaluated without `./m`, and a barrel file re-exporting forty modules depends on forty. Pre-fix the dependency was recorded ONLY in ParseResult.imports, which reaches the brain_import TABLE (parallel-indexer.ts:2168, insertImport), and never as a relationship, which reaches brain_relationship (:2174) — two separate statements over two shapes, with no consumer reconciling them. So a barrel file appeared to depend on nothing in the graph bb_graph, bb_impact and bb_migrate read. Measured with script/m14/ts-construct-probe.ts over tracked .ts files of bb_tests/repositories/typescript, production path, first 40 files: `export … from` occurs in 14 of them (86 named, 13 star, 1 export-assignment) and ZERO published an imports edge; the star form published no exports edge either, so a pure barrel contributed no relationship at all. Corpus probe after the fix: export-star-from 3 of 13 leaf-sites covered before (and those 3 were false credits from a probe bug now fixed), 13 of 13 after. THE FORBIDS ARE THE POINT: `exports: barrel -> "*"` is refused on purpose, because `*` names no symbol — the unresolvable-endpoint class the family rules out for anonymous constructors (X8) and placeholder literals (R7). An `export {} from` clause is pinned to publish nothing, because an empty binding list asserts nothing about the module's evaluation, unlike a bare `import "./x"` which does.

expectRelationships.note: THE GAIN: a named re-export is a dependency on ./vendor/alpha for the name `alpha`. Same `path:item` shape a static import uses, so one consumer rule covers both

the item is the name ASKED FOR (`beta`), not the name published (`renamedBeta`). An alias is what THIS file calls the binding; the name is what the exporting module calls it, and only the second can be joined against that module. The exports edge below carries `renamedBeta` — the two halves answer different questions and conflating them asks a module for a name it does not export
the STAR form, in the whole-module shape the analyzer already uses for a namespace import and for a side-effect import

`export * as ns from` takes the MODULE ITSELF under the alias `ns`, so the dependency is the whole-module `*` shape — the same target a namespace import publishes, because it asks exactly as much of the module. The `*` token is INSIDE namespace_export, so a bare token check on the statement misses this shape entirely
`export type { … } from` — a TYPE-only re-export is still a module dependency: the type cannot be checked without the module
the CONTROL: an ordinary static import, unchanged by this fix. Pinned so the re-export rows cannot be mistaken for the static-import path having moved
the export half, unchanged: the EXPORTED name, alias when there is one

forbidRelationships.note: THE REFUSAL, PINNED. `export * from "./m"` re-exports a set this file cannot name, and an exports edge needs a NAME. Shipping `exports: barrel -> "*"` would be the X8/R7 unresolvable-endpoint class, and pool-worker's angle-bracket filter is not what would stop it — `*` passes every universal target rule

forbidden on purpose: `export { beta as renamedBeta } from "./m"` publishes the name `renamedBeta` (pinned above), so an edge to `beta` would name a symbol this module does not publish — the exported name is the alias, and the source name belongs to the other module

`export {} from "./m"` has an EMPTY binding list. It is not a dependency-for-side-effects the way `import "./m"` is, and the analyzer already distinguishes the two — the side-effect rule keys on an ABSENT import_clause, not on an empty item list

the module path and the item name belong to the same STATEMENT. An earlier version of the re-export import collector re-scanned the global exports array by line-range overlap and fabricated exactly this cross-module pairing when two export statements shared a line

THE DEFECT THIS FIXTURE CAUGHT IN ITS OWN AUTHOR'S FIRST CUT. The dependency edge published the PUBLISHED name, so it asked `./vendor/beta` for `renamedBeta` — a name that module does not export, i.e. an endpoint no index can join. Found by writing the oracle (script/m14/oracles/typescript-imports-exports.ts), whose import rule states the opposite in as many words: 'an ALIAS is not part of the name, because the alias is what THIS file calls it and the name is what the exporting module calls it'. A gate that had been watching this label would have caught it; this label had none, which is the DERIVATION finding IMPORTS_ENUM is about.
